did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter describes how the covenant was made and written down, rather than remaining merely an oral commitment.
Did you know? Nehemiah the governor is listed first among those who signed the covenant, followed by Zedekiah.
Did you know? After Nehemiah and Zedekiah, a list of the priests who signed the covenant appears, including Seraiah, Azariah, and Jeremiah.
Did you know? The Levites also signed the covenant; among them were Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui, and Kadmiel.
Did you know? After the priests and Levites, the leaders of the people also signed, representing the families of Israel.
Did you know? The rest of the people joined the covenant under oath, pledging to follow God’s law and keep His commandments, ordinances, and statutes.
Did you know? The covenant included a commitment not to buy goods on the Sabbath or on holy days, and to observe the sabbatical year and cancel debts.
Did you know? The people agreed to contribute one-third of a shekel each year for the service of the house of God, to provide for the needs of the temple and the offerings.
Did you know? The supply of wood for the altar was arranged by casting lots among the priests, Levites, and people, according to a fixed schedule each year.
Did you know? The commitments conclude with the explicit declaration, “We will not neglect the house of our God”—a continuing commitment to maintaining and serving the temple.
